items.title: Coordination EventRecord family and event-key vocabulary
items.statement: The registry defines a seglog-backed coordination event family whose key vocabulary covers registration, status, operation, file ownership, unregister, crash, abort, and debug-mirror export events.

items.title: Per-event payload contracts are intentionally deferred
items.statement: Only schema_version is universally required while all identity, revision, operation, path, and checkpoint fields are optional, and the registry explicitly defers full payload schemas. The authoritative window therefore cannot determine which fields are mandatory for any named event or how an implementation rejects malformed event-specific payloads.
items.impact: Independent writers and readers can choose incompatible payload requirements, preventing deterministic implementation or validation of registration, ownership, crash, abort, and mirror-export records.
items.builder_discretion: A builder would have to invent per-event discriminators, required field sets, field types, invariants, and invalid-record handling until the deferred schema is reopened.

items.title: Event replay, duplicate prevention, and stale-update prevention
items.statement: Coordination events replay in seglog order into redb projections, with idempotency keys and expected revisions designated to prevent duplicate or stale updates.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Coordination events replay in seglog order into coordination redb projections; idempotency keys and expected revisions prevent duplicate or stale updates.",

items.title: Replay conflict and recovery semantics are unspecified
items.statement: The replay rule names seglog order, idempotency keys, and expected revisions but does not define the ordering scope, idempotency-key uniqueness scope or lifetime, the comparison rule for revisions, or the outcome and recovery path when a duplicate, gap, or stale revision is detected.
items.impact: Projectors may diverge on whether to ignore, quarantine, retry, halt, or surface conflicting records, which can propagate inconsistent scheduling and prompt context.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must select conflict detection scopes, terminal/error states, retry policy, quarantine behavior, and observability for replay failures.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Coordination events replay in seglog order into coordination redb projections; idempotency keys and expected revisions prevent duplicate or stale updates.",

items.title: Coordination lifecycle transitions and event-specific authority are absent
items.statement: The family names status, operation, ownership, unregister, crash, and abort events and lists three broad producers, but it does not define legal source states, destination states, terminality, side effects, or which producer is authorized to emit each event.
items.impact: Schedulers and conflict-prevention consumers cannot deterministically decide whether a transition is legal or whether ownership, operation, or agent state must be released after crash, abort, or unregister.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must invent the lifecycle state machine, transition guards, event precedence, producer permissions, and release/cleanup effects.

items.statement: The window requires readers to verify checkpoint coverage but does not define the compared watermark or scope, acceptable lag, atomic read protocol, failure result, timeout, retry/rebuild behavior, or whether scheduling and prompt assembly fail closed.

items.title: Projection value schemas and consistency invariants are deferred
items.statement: The projection family requires only schema_version, makes all key-correlating and checkpoint fields optional, and explicitly defers materialized projection schemas. items.impact: Readers cannot validate a row against its key or prove that agent, file, operation, snapshot, and checkpoint views represent the same event prefix.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must invent projection record shapes, required identity fields, transactional batching, checkpoint commit order, and partial-write recovery.

items.impact: A compatibility reader can silently become an authority path and bypass checkpoint coverage, canonical replay, and stale-state protections.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must invent enforcement at APIs or type boundaries and an acceptance test detecting prohibited authoritative reads.

dimension_assessments.summary: Replay, rebuild, and mirror regeneration behaviors are named, but conflict, stale-read, and failure behavior remains under-specified.
The three storage families and their coarse capabilities are present, while concrete runtime payload and materialized projection capability is explicitly deferred.
Producers, consumers, key vocabularies, and mirror paths are identified, but event-specific payload and output-value requirements are not.
Storage kinds, versions, encodings, keys, redaction, and authority boundaries are stated; deferred value schemas prevent complete executable contracts.
Lifecycle event names exist without legal state transitions, guards, terminality, precedence, or release effects.
Seglog is canonical and mirrors are non-authoritative, but per-event emit authority and mirror-boundary enforcement are missing.
Owner documents and deferred owners are explicit for event, projection, and mirror families.
Scheduler, AgentCoordinator, prompt assembler, projector, exporter, inspection, debug, and interoperability consumers are named.
Inspection views are named and the tier anticipates later GUI projection, but no user-visible behavior or freshness/error presentation is defined here.
Rebuildability and canonical recovery sources are stated, but conflict, partial projection, checkpoint failure, and mirror-export recovery are not executable.
Strong no-secret and path-redaction rules are explicit, but the window supplies no validation oracle or failure handling for redaction enforcement.
Event-to-projection-to-consumer-to-mirror propagation is described, but transactional boundaries, freshness gates, and prohibited mirror-authority propagation lack concrete enforcement.
Retention and rebuild intent exist, while observability, alerting, safe degradation, quarantine operations, and operator recovery controls are absent.
No capacity, throughput, latency, checkpoint-lag, replay, compaction, or storage-growth budgets are stated.
Legacy files are constrained to compatibility/debug use and mirrors are migration-only, but import, cutover, convergence, and decommission mechanics are missing.
The window has no bound fixtures or executable pass/fail oracles for payloads, encoding, replay, projection freshness, migration, redaction, or mirror non-authority.
Builders retain consequential choices over payloads, lifecycle semantics, replay conflicts, checkpoint gating, transactions, migration, exports, performance, and operations.
The main unknowns are the explicitly deferred payload/projection schemas plus unresolved lifecycle, consistency, migration, GUI, scaling, validation, and operational semantics.
